mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted by markets as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which reduces the present value of future earnings for large-cap firms and thus drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS average > 4% over the past quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4%, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test against baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: No statistically significant correlation (p > 0.1) between PAYEMS/UNRATE movements and 60-day forward returns in 5 consecutive tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above the prior quarter's level indicates a turning point in supply-side constraints, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls then rises above previous quarter value
failure_condition: INDPRO shows no clear turning point (3 consecutive quarters of decline) or 20-day returns remain negative when the signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds consensus forecasts by more than 0.5%, it reflects accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to signal tighter policy, which compresses equity discount rates and yields negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > forecast + 0.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL surprises are present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months, despite low interest rates, signals weakening construction activity that reduces economic momentum and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively correlated with HOUST declines (Spearman's rho < -0.2) during multi-month declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains above 5% for two consecutive months despite steady job growth (PAYEMS), it indicates a labor market that is neither expanding nor contracting vigorously, which often coincides with risk aversion and negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS stable while UNRATE > 5% for two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05) during such labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in consumer confidence indices (not available in the provided catalog; therefore this sketch is invalid per the rules) — thus, instead: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) for three months suggests resilient demand across sectors, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to outperform a 5% confidence interval around the mean during such demand expansions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 1% for four consecutive months in a context of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), it creates a policy divergence where markets anticipate future tightening, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 4 months and CPIAUCSL rising
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the policy divergence is present.
